Headteachers’ Welcome
The Frances Bardsley Academy for Girls is an excellent school and has provided an exemplary education for girls aged eleven to eighteen for over one hundred years. In 1906, Miss Frances Bardsley was determined to offer girls in the local area a first class education and the opportunity to develop their skills, abilities and self confidence. We share her vision and as a school, our mission is clear:
“The Frances Bardsley Academy exists to empower young women with the knowledge and personal characteristics needed to live successful and fulfilling lives.”
Our expectations are high because we believe in being aspirational. Pupils make excellent progress at the school and our results are above the national average. In July 2019 Ofsted called our school, “a purposeful, safe, welcoming and happy environment” with “confident, courteous and articulate” students. They praised the fact that pupils, parents and staff are proud to be part of our community. Through working with the best girls’ schools in the UK and abroad, we have developed our holistic approach which supports the physical, moral and spiritual development of our girls.
The pupils study a broad and balanced curriculum and we continue to offer a wide range of creative subjects alongside more traditional academic ones. We want our pupils to flourish and develop a love for learning. Throughout and beyond the school day, we offer an extensive range of clubs and activities in our enrichment and extracurricular programme. We have a farm, an art gallery and a railway, and run numerous trips and visits each year. In addition to this we have our purpose built Platform to provide individuals and groups with tailored support for any challenges they may face.
As founder of the dynamic LIFE Education Trust we work collaboratively with schools in Havering and Essex and are fully committed to the LIFE vision: “Building Great Learning Communities.”
We are proud of this wonderful school, empowering young women to flourish academically and socially for a successful future. As leaders, we look forward to welcoming you and your daughter here.
Emilie Darabasz(Headteacher)
David Turrell(Executive Headteacher)

British Values
At FBA we believe British Values are the shared values of all our communities.
We are all very proud of our school and our community of students, employees, parents, carers and Governors who work together to provide an outstanding learning environment.
Every one of our 1413 students is valued equally as an individual with different gifts and talents.
At FBA, we value the diversity of background of all students, families and the wider school community.
The Department for Education states that: “Schools should promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs. Actively promoting the values means challenging opinions or behaviours in school that are contrary to fundamental British values”.
The Department for Education defines British Values as follows:
Our school reflects British values in all that we do. We encourage our children to be creative, unique, open-minded and independent individuals, respectful of themselves and of others in our school, our local community and the wider world.
We promote values of democracy, respect and harmony for all races, cultures, faiths and beliefs.
The school promotes equal opportunities for all and systems are in place that counter racism, sexism and all other forms of discrimination and extremism whenever they occur.

Languages Translation Bee – Regional Final Event
Last week, FBA hosted the Routes into Languages Translation Bee – Regional Final event. Our 4 student finalists did really well and should be very proud of themselves and the fact that they were part of the final 63 out of the 3,834 students who started the competition in London.• Muskan Khan• Livia Vince• Dhiksha Gobinathan• Alina QureshiWe are pleased to announce that Dhiksha came 2nd in French, and is going through to the National Final at Cambridge University on Monday 30th June!
Huge thanks to our dream team of Year 12 Prefects, as well as 2 previous Translation Bee participants (Carys H and Lilia W in Year 11), who helped with the organisation:• Diya Patel• Chloe Watkins• Shaan Dhadwar• Farah Beddal• Alexia Axinte• Ramisha Choudhury• Jenika Mudhar• Sophie PotterAnd to our colleagues from the Language Department for organizing this very successful event. It reminded us that learning a new language is like unlocking a door to a world of new experiences, perspectives, and connections. As Federico Fellini once said, “A different language is a different vision of life.”

pageCache.pageTitle: Matilda the Musical At FBA - The Frances Bardsley Academy For Girls The Frances Bardsley Academy For Girls

Matilda the Musical At FBA
In March, our school community came together for two incredible evenings of entertainment as our students brought Matilda the Musical to life on stage. It was a true showcase of talent, dedication, and teamwork, and we could not be prouder of everyone involved.
A huge thank you to our talented students, whose hard work and passion shone through in every scene, song, and dance. From our lead performers to the ensemble, backstage crew, and tech team – each of you played a vital role in making the show a success. Your commitment and creativity were truly inspiring!
We also extend our deepest gratitude to our dedicated colleagues who devoted countless hours to rehearsals and all the behind-the-scenes details that made this production possible. Your guidance and encouragement helped our students shine!
A heartfelt thank you as well to our wonderful parents and families for your support and your attendance. Your presence made these performances even more special.
To everyone who contributed to this unforgettable production—thank you. The hard work, teamwork, and passion on display remind us of the incredible creativity and spirit within our school community. Bravo to all!

pageCache.pageTitle: GCSE Results 2026 - The Frances Bardsley Academy For Girls The Frances Bardsley Academy For Girls
pageCache.text:
GCSE Results 2026
We are delighted to be celebrating an excellent set of GCSE results for the Class of 2026, reflecting the hard work, determination and ambition of our Year 11 students.
This year, an impressive 79% of all exam entries were graded 9–4, while results in English and Maths were particularly strong, with 55.7% of students achieving Grade 5 or above in both subjects and 73% achieving Grade 4 or above. These results represent a significant improvement on last year and are a fantastic achievement for our students and the whole Frances Bardsley community.
However, results are much more than statistics. Behind every grade is a story ofhard work, perseverance and determination, and we are incredibly proud ofeverything our Year 11 students have achieved.
We look forward to welcoming students to Frances Bardsley Sixth Form in September, where they will take the next exciting step in their education.
Headteacher Emilie Darabasz and Executive Headteacher David Turrell said:
“We would like to thank our exceptional staff and our students’ families for the encouragement and support they have given along the way. We are very excited towelcome students back to our Sixth Form, but we are equally proud of thoseheading to other schools, colleges, apprenticeships and other new opportunities. We wish every one of them enormous success for the future. Congratulations, Class of 2026!”
